_what: AMENDED acceptance for the GPU rerank path, registered BEFORE the recovery measurements it judges.
_supersedes: the determinism gate in PREREGISTRATION-gpu.json. That registration's OTHER gates -- provider assertion by get_providers() AND node placement -- are UNCHANGED and still binding.
_authority: the human, explicitly: 'This is a design decision on my authority, and it needs its own ADR -- cite the spike as evidence, not as authorisation.'

what_had_been_observed: G0 CPU seq 1t p50 200.124 ms/slate, G3 repeat 200.530, noise floor 0.406 ms
G2 CUDA batched p50 2.877 ms/slate -- 70x the CPU arm
cross-provider logit delta: G1 max 0.00210666656, G2 max 0.00218200684
both CUDA cells ran 13.6% of nodes on CPU (55,680 of 408,320)
NOTHING about whether the delta reorders a slate, whether GPU-to-GPU repeatability is recoverable, or which ops fall back.

why_the_original_gate_is_amended_rather_.the_argument: bit-identity across providers existed to make OPTIMIZATION MEASUREMENTS COMPARABLE -- so that a latency change could be attributed to the change rather than to a moved scorer. At 2.877 ms against a 300 ms budget there is no optimization space left to protect. The instrument outlived the thing it was instrumenting.
why_the_original_gate_is_amended_rather_.the_driver: brief section 9 requires 800 ms voice-to-voice P50 with retrieval INSIDE that budget. 200 ms of a 300 ms retrieval budget inside an 800 ms conversational budget was never going to work. 2.877 ms does.
why_the_original_gate_is_amended_rather_.what_this_is_NOT: this is not a tolerance sought after a gate failed. The gate is replaced by a DIFFERENT gate that tests the property that still matters -- ranking -- and a STRICTER one where determinism is still recoverable.
why_the_original_gate_is_amended_rather_.the_spike_is_evidence_not_authorisation: the 70x number is why the question was asked. It does not by itself license the change; the design decision and its ADR do.

gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_byte_identity.requirement: repeated CUDA runs must be BIT-IDENTICAL to one another
gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_byte_identity.status: THE BAR. Within a provider, determinism is a property the system should have and may be recoverable.
what_will_be_swept: cudnn_conv_algo_search = HEURISTIC and DEFAULT (EXHAUSTIVE autotunes and is expected to be the least reproducible)
gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_byte_identity.usual_causes_named_in_advance: nondeterministic kernel selection and atomic reductions
gate_1_gpu_to_gpu_byte_identity.verdict_if_unrecoverable: report it plainly. A nondeterministic scorer is a real cost and must be visible in the ADR, not absorbed.

gate_2_cross_provider_is_RANKING_EQUIVAL.requirement: the top-10 ORDER must match CPU on the held-out set
gate_2_cross_provider_is_RANKING_EQUIVAL.rationale: the slate IS the depth-10 top-10, so order equivalence over it is exactly what determines R@1, R@5 and R@10. A logit delta that never reorders is a different fact from one that does, and the acceptance is written against that distinction.
also_reported_because_it_is_not_the_same: is 0.0021 a WORST CASE or a MEDIAN? the distribution of |delta|, not just its max
how many slates reorder at all
whether R@1 over the held-out set moves by even one case
gate_2_cross_provider_is_RANKING_EQUIVAL.verdict_if_ranking_equivalence_ALSO_fail: REPORT IT AND STOP. That is a different and more serious finding than a logit delta -- it means the two paths disagree about what to retrieve, and no amount of speed makes two paths that retrieve differently into one system.

gate_3_node_fallback.requirement: identify the ops in the 13.6% running on CPU
gate_3_node_fallback.why_it_is_both: a correctness surface -- every fallback is a boundary where two providers' numerics meet mid-graph -- AND speed left on the table.

open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver._status: OPEN GAP with a named closing condition. NOT a caveat.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.what_was_verified: node placement was measured ONCE, in Python, on THIS graph, at ORT 1.24.2: 13.6% of nodes ran on CPU under a registered CUDA session -- 55,680 of 408,320.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.what_the_census_is_evidence_FOR: the CURRENT placement is benign -- every fallback op is a shape or index operation and there is not a single matmul among them, which is why 13.6% of NODES costs so little TIME.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.what_it_is_NOT_evidence_for: that it will STAY benign. It is a snapshot of one graph at one ORT version.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.the_limitation: `ort` exposes no node enumeration, so the SHIPPED Rust binary cannot re-verify placement. `error_on_failure()` covers provider REGISTRATION only. A future graph change, model swap, or ORT upgrade could move matmuls onto the CPU fallback and NOTHING would report it -- the run would simply be slower, and a slower run reads as machine drift, which this session has shown is large enough to hide it.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.closing_condition: either `ort` exposes node placement, or a Rust-side profiling hook is added that reads ORT's profiling output the way tools/session_l_gpu_recovery.py does. Until one of those exists, this is open.
open_gap_node_placement_cannot_be_re_ver.interim_obligation: re-run tools/session_l_gpu_recovery.py after ANY change to the graph, the model, or the ORT version. The verification does not survive those on its own.

what_ships.cpu: STAYS the fallback and stays shipped where no GPU exists.
what_ships.two_paths: both correct, both measured, and the difference DOCUMENTED rather than hidden.
what_ships.the_hazard_being_accepted_deliberately: two numeric paths where one ships and one is measured is a configuration this project has been burned by. It is accepted here with eyes open because the alternative is a 200 ms retrieval stage inside an 800 ms conversational budget. The mitigation is that BOTH are measured and the difference is published, not that the difference is small.
what_ships.unchanged_regardless: rerank::SHIPPED_THREADS = 1 on the CPU path. Threading remains a +158.9 ms regression and this amendment says nothing about it.
